script: My passport vanished after I donated the book that hid it. . I slipped my passport into the heaviest cookbook I owned, then piled a stack of other books on top because my drawer was overpacked and my passport was slightly bent. The weight smoothed it out so well, I didn't even notice it was still there. (Micro‑hook: "I didn't even notice it was still there.") Fast forward a few weeks—while I was clearing out the kitchen, I grabbed a box of cookbooks to donate to a charity shop. I didn't think twice; I was already saving up for that trip I've been livestreaming on Kick. Later that day, I started packing, and bam, my passport was MIA. I tore through my apartment, looking for the missing ID, and then it hit me—my genius passport‑flattening system. (Micro‑hook: "Then it hit me—my genius passport‑flattening system.") I called the shop. The cookbook was already sold. I was like, "I can't believe I just gave my identity to a stranger." The clerk said the buyer found my passport next to a beef stew recipe and had contacted the shop. They returned it to me, but the buyer asked why I used government docs as bookmarks. (Stakes: I risked my identity, my travel plans, and the integrity of my docs.) I got my passport back, but the whole thing felt like a lesson: don't let your passport become a culinary prop. TL;DR I flattened my passport inside a cookbook, forgot it, donated the book, and accidentally let a stranger hold my ID with 200 soup recipes. (End)
